Lang-Gan

Like other angels, Zibai was born in accordance with a divine plan of the Heavenly Principles. Thus, she appeared beneath the skies of Teyvat, bearing the mantle of the heavens' mission. One day, the shadow of a king, the
placed before Zibai a crest engraved with the sigil of the moons. Its meaning was that she would no longer be just an agent of the morning stars but would become an envoy of the moons as well. Although she didn't accept that crest, she began to travel back and forth, from the morning stars to the moons to the earth. She was assigned to lead the people of a kingdom that existed in the territory of the modern Chasm, known as
Its settlements stretched from peak to peak, and life was centered around the mines. The kingdom, rich in Sand Crystals and gemstones, became the pearl of a unified civilization. Zibai taught the people to till and weave, and, as a result, they prospered with bountiful harvests, their granaries close to bursting. Therefore, the people of that ancient kingdom worshipped her as the God of Soil and Grain and sent her their wishes into the sky in the form of lanterns, praying for good fortune and blessings in the coming year.

<color=#ffffffd9>"As the Eternal Moon rises in the night sky, a maiden adorned with lustrous jade descends upon the earth. She blesses the kudzu vines and mulberry leaves, so that they may be used to make coarse cloth that is nevertheless soft, light, and comfortable to wear."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"As the Iridescent Moon rises in the night sky, a maiden adorned with lustrous jade descends upon the earth. She blesses the kudzu vines and hemp, so that they may be used to make fine, luxurious cloth."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"As the Frost Moon rises in the night sky, a maiden adorned with lustrous jade descends upon the earth. She blesses the mugwort and artemisia, so that they may be perfect for divination."</color>

Understanding her mission well, the emissary began to cultivate the soil: if the soil is fertile, the
would flourish, but if the soil were spoiled, the
would become a putrid swamp. Flowers tainted with putrescence must be uprooted with the soil, lest they profane the heavens' love. The Heavenly Principles did not worry about
that were not sacred, even if it would turn them to pure nothingness. Over time, the angel noticed that the love of the Heavenly Principles and the Moons for this garden was not equal. The silver moonlight preferred to offer solace to those who had suffered the withering light. Zibai was occasionally assailed by doubts: whose will and love were more sacred? She knew that the divine plan of the Heavenly Principles was most sacred, but for some reason, she was drawn closer to the love of the moons, and she lingered longer and longer in the small
that she tended herself. One day, she heard how the civilization her colleague tended had profaned the divine and was completely destroyed. Sorrow washed over her, but it soon turned to unease. Zibai couldn't understand the cause of her sadness, for heaven's mission didn't include such a feeling. Had the will and love she once bore lost their sanctity? At that moment, Zibai's fate changed course, and one of the shades of the Heavenly Principles, the
looked over her.

When the war, known as the War of the Funerary Flame, between the Heavenly Principles and the primeval creator of this world, Nibelung, began in Teyvat about six thousand years ago, the earth collapsed, and the world was turned upside down. The shockwaves of that catastrophe, laden with dark malice, crashed over Lang-Gan, followed by the firm intention of the Heavenly Principles to begin a purge. A sacred will coalesced as though divine punishment descended upon the ancient kingdom in the form of a sky-blue
in an attempt to scour its tainted land from the world. To secure a glimmer of hope for the people she watched over, Zibai defied the will of the heavens and protected people from the Spiritstone. Thanks to her, survivors of Lang-Gan traveled north and built their new home in Chenyu Vale. And although the Ruler of Time warned the moon envoy that she would disappear along with her kingdom, Zibai was ready to die with them as their goddess. Istaroth didn't understand the angel's desire to sacrifice herself for the people. As a result, Zibai's spirit was sundered into three fragments. Yet, whether stirred by pity or to punish an act of betrayal, a shade of time watching from the heavens above extended a hand to Zibai. From that moment on, Zibai's three severed spirits have been frozen in that fleeting instant, a fraction of a second before their dissipation, and her essence wanders eternally in a dream where both life and death are beyond reach.

customize.text: Three Deadly Selves

When Zibai descended to the mortal world as the moon envoy, she encountered a mystical being, Morax, whose powers were comparable to those of a god. The being was not an angel, had a human form and beautiful features, but could fly in the clouds, move mountains, fill the seas, shatter rocks, and crush jade. One day, Zibai and Morax decided to have a friendly duel in the Adeptal Arts. When the time came, Morax was nowhere to be seen, but a rumble was heard high in the sky. Following the sound, Zibai saw three identical figures battling each other in the clouds. Soon, the battle ended, and the three shadows merged into one again, descending before the heavenly messenger. It was Morax. The Lord of Geo revealed an ancient technique of "Tri-Factor Excision," or how to excise the "Three Deadly Selves." The Three Deadly Selves represent impure thoughts and corrupt desires in the practitioner's mind, and cutting them off allows one to realize one's true self. Because Zibai was an emissary of heaven, she had no corrupt desires or false thoughts, and no matter how hard she tried, she could not sever the Three Deadly Selves. Morax told her that the will of heaven shifts and does not stay, while white clouds drift and turn to hounds of grey. And he was absolutely right: when Zibai saw heavenly punishment descend upon her kingdom, resentment, fear, and sadness began to corrode her soul. And at that very moment, she was able to sever the Three Deadly Selves, which were to serve as a means of resisting heaven. And it was at that very moment that the shade of Time descended upon her, sealing her in time. In the last moment before her death, Istaroth preserved the moon envoy's soul essence and placed it within the Three Deadly Selves.

Zibai's First Deadly Self was named Ziju, and she was closest to the true nature of the moon envoy herself. The soul fragment contained within her was the Heavenly Soul, also known as Taiguang. After Zibai's death, her First Deadly Self ascended to the heavens and became one with the shadowmoon. People say that a day in the heavens is equivalent to a century on earth, but perhaps the opposite is true. Ziju spent countless hours in the moon prison, and it felt as if a single day in the mortal world lasted a hundred years. Her memories were erased, and only vague images remained: Lang-Gan, Ziju, people's voices and faces, lanterns.

Zibai's Second Deadly Self was named Zizhi, and she inherited the most memories and wisdom. The soul fragment contained within her was the Earth Soul, also known as Shuangling. This fragment of Zibai's soul was born from her anger and regret at being unable to save the people of her kingdom. After Zibai's death, her Second Deadly Self fell into a slumber deep beneath the earth in what is now known as The Chasm, merging with the jade carriage. When the true Frost Moon was returned to the false heavens of Teyvat six thousand years later, it awakened again, seeking to fulfill the desires of the people, no matter the cost.

Zibai's Third Deadly Self was named Zijiao, and she was the most free-spirited among the three. The soul fragment contained within her was the Human Soul named Youjing. During the Archon War, Rex Lapis freed her from a silk painting of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer and forged a contract with her, obliging her to aid him in battle. Together, they subdued Chenyu Vale and brought peace to Mt. Qingce. During the Archon War, there was a divine mountain in Liyue with a giant tree on its summit. This tree was a god named "Tao Dou," originally known as "Bune." Back then, people thought that behind Tao Dou was the realm of the dead, and if you committed grave sins in life, your soul would be unable to pass beyond that tree and into the afterlife.

About two to three thousand years ago, the Eight Adepts rose up — eight people and beasts who laid down a great magic array to purify Tao Dou. He cared greatly for all living things and volunteered to sanctify himself to pacify the underworld. Tao Dou was sealed in a secret palace in the Qingce Mountains called the "Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula" along with other evil spirits, and the palace itself was enchanted using the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Array. After that, Tao Dou's remains sank into the Ley Lines and became a border, separating the living of Liyue from the dead in Liyue. The mortals continued to preserve and maintain the god's new form for thousands of years. Zijiao joined the Eight Adepts under the name Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare, one of the Three Beasts of Tao Dou, also known as the Three Immortals of Tao Dou. The other two beasts included the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame, which sacrificed itself during the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Array, and the Jade-Plumed
The other Adepts were the Three Hermits of Guizang: "Wind Reader," "Yunlai Angler," and the Wuwang Kid, as well as the Two Sages of Lianshan: Sage Hu and Sage Jian. After the purification of Tao Dou, Silverwing and Wind Reader traveled together, and the white horse went to live in seclusion in the Qingce mountain range.

The traces of time left on Zijiao by Istaroth exerted an inexplicable influence on the ancient Geo Archon. After the Archon War, recognizing the threat she posed, she hid in the mountains and forests, only occasionally appearing to humans to demonstrate her abilities. Since mortals barely lived for a hundred years, they were virtually immune to the ravages of time, and from time to time, the White Horse Adeptus would appear to those in need. By aiding them in their time of need, she also sought to pass on to posterity stories of the days before the sky fell and the earth opened up.

customize.text: Zibai's Revival

When the true Frost Moon, banished beyond the false sky by the Heavenly Principles during the War of the Funerary Flame, was returned to Teyvat, the false moon where Ziju was imprisoned began to crumble. When this process occurred, people saw the moon obscured by a black shadow. When it stopped, the black shadow disappeared, becoming invisible to the naked eye. It was this process that people associated with the Moon Devourer. The moon's disintegration was influenced by the wishes of people, which were once granted by the White Horse Adeptus. Over countless years, Ziju merged with the shadowmoon, and on the day of Lantern Rite, when people made their wishes, the shadowmoon would disappear, and with it, Ziju would cease to exist. This would have completely destroyed the fragment of Zibai's soul, but it also provided an opportunity to free her from the moon's projection. The divine messenger's old friend, Rex Lapis, decided to unite the Three Deadly Selves to revive her. When the relics of the destroyed Lang-Gan were delivered to Liyue, an exhibition was held, at which Morax asked the Traveler to take the jade token that once belonged to Zibai. Thanks to the Moon Goddess's blessing, the Traveler was able to find themselves in the prison of Ziju, who was unable to reach the end of it. The Traveler's connection to the Moons confirmed the Lord of Geo's suspicions, and he asked for their help in finding the Second Deadly Self, Zizhi.

When Zizhi awoke in The Chasm and possessed an archaeologist named Lu Xiangxiang, she saw through the mortal girl's eyes the pure and clear moon, unchanged for thousands of years. She wished to fulfill the mortal's wish: to become the most renowned archaeologist in Teyvat. Under the influence of the entity, Lu Xiangxiang traveled to the Chenyu Vale, where she took a photograph of a "lunar eclipse," the overlap of a decaying false moon and the real one. She then went to a restaurant, where she attacked people. When the Traveler and the Ministry of Civil Affairs went to search for Lu Xiangxiang, Zizhi was forced to possess another person. When she was finally cornered, and the only one she could possess was the Traveler, the Deadly Self agreed to answer their questions if they escaped the timestream. In her prison, she recounted the destruction of the kingdom of Lang-Gan and her rage and regret at not being able to save more people. When Zizhi learned that, thanks to her sacrifice, Lang-Gan's descendants were thriving in Liyue, her rage subsided, and she agreed to surrender the fragment of Zibai's soul that was stored within her. Knowing that Zizhi would then disappear, the Traveler offered to make a final wish.

<color=#ffffffd9>"In regard to my fate, and that of Lang-Gan's fallen... I know there is little I can demand of you.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>However, should another raise a war banner against the heavens someday, let my name be set upon its cloth.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I ask for this, and nothing more.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Now, take what you came for.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I was a lone moon, shrouded and dimmed in cloud-veiled night.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Now darkness breaks, free and unburdened, I reclaim my light."</color>

While the Traveler was recovering the soul fragment from the Second Deadly Self, Rex Lapis went to search for the Third Deadly Self, Zijiao. This Deadly Self had no interest in the Lang-Gan's past and considered herself a different being from Zibai, so she refused to hand over the moon envoy's soul fragment. When Rex Lapis was ready to leave, Zijiao stopped him, asking if he should offer her a new contract she couldn't refuse. He then suggested that she see the world for herself and go to Liyue Harbor for the Lantern Rite festival, and that she would be led by two guides, the Traveler and Paimon. Although Zijiao considered a tour of Liyue too small a price to pay for her existence, she agreed. First, Zijiao, the Traveler, and Paimon went to eat at the Wanmin Restaurant, where they met Lu Xiangxiang. They learned from the girl that she had joined the archaeological team by chance and didn't know what she wanted to do with her life. They then went to listen to stories from Iron Tongue Tian, where they met the leader of the Yun Opera, Yun Jin. She and the storyteller discussed "An Ancient Poem" found on the relics from The Chasm. Zijiao recited the poem in full and told Yun Jin its true title. Afterward, the Traveler and Paimon led Zijiao to the Mingxiao Lantern created in her honor. There, the other two Adepti, Ganyu and Yanfei, told them about a new legend about the White Horse Adeptus. Liyue celebrates the festival of the Stove God, Marchosius, but originally, there was a ritual called the Moonchase Rite, conducted by the Lord of Geo himself. It turned out that this ritual was an appeal to the White Horse Adeptus, but during the entire time it was performed, she never responded.

Zijiao had previously believed that no one remembered her existence, but Rex Lapis had been trying to bring back his old friend for all these millennia, and the people the White Horse Adeptus had met had preserved all her stories. When she entered the city, she saw porters passing through the alleys, setting down heavy wooden crates from their weary shoulders; peddlers pushing carts, as the kites and lanterns upon them rustled gently in the breeze. Cooks cooking, actors acting, scholars reading, soldiers marching, children playing, elders resting, officials officiating, and the common folk absorbed in this or that, reveling in the simple joys of life. Some, it seems, had already found that which stirred their hearts, while others continued to fret, troubled by uncertain futures. However, in this calm and serene order, everyone eagerly awaited the arrival of the celebrations and the first light of the morrow. What she had once longed to see in the kingdom of Lang-Gan appeared before her thousands of years later in Liyue Harbor. And although Zijiao knew that without Zibai's soul fragment, her Deadly Self would vanish, she gave it to the Traveler.

During Lantern Rite, when people launched Xiao Lantern with wishes and prayers to the White Horse Adeptus, the false moon where Zibai's Heavenly Soul was imprisoned finally shattered. Rex Lapis and the Traveler combined all the fragments of the angel's soul, and she was reborn in Liyue. Her consciousness was intertwined with the personalities and memories of her Three Deadly Selves, so she had no memory of herself or those around her. To help Zibai leave traces in Liyue that time could not erase, Morax sent her to buy tea in Chenyu Vale, a place she had never visited before. Along the way, she met the Traveler and Paimon, and they set out on another tour of Liyue. The angel recreated the moon chariot used by the Moon Goddesses to show them the view from above. And although she still doesn't remember much about her life, she began to make friends to leave her mark on this world.

customize.text: Legends

Many legends of Liyue make mention of a mysterious White Horse Adeptus. Traces of her story are scattered throughout books and folktales, but her appearance is described differently in different sources. The elders of Qingce Village say she became a steed as white as snow and, in the days of the Archon War, aided Rex Lapis in attaining supremacy over the mortal realm. In the Chenyu Vale, she is considered the "daughter of time." Some believe her to be the Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare from "The Sanctification of Tao Dou." Others whisper that her eyes, as amber touched with gold, hold the power to gaze through the desolate wastelands of time itself. And the last insists she has always lived on the moon, listening to the wishes of mortals, and keeping watch over the world of flickering lights below. And although people call her an Adeptus, she did not receive this title from the Prime of Adepti, Morax, but was named so by people.

One legend about the White Horse Adeptus tells of a boy lost in a bamboo forest. There, the boy encountered a slender woman garbed in white. She stood beside a clear babbling brook, with beads of water glistening on her woven rush raincoat, her golden eyes melding with the rays cast through the forest by the setting sun. The boy told her he wanted to go on an adventure, sail across the seas, and witness the stone spears of the Lord of Geo with his own eyes. But as soon as he emerged, he became lost. The woman laughed and extended her hand to lead him out of the forest. Her skin was cold and damp to the touch, much like fresh rain upon a mountain or dewdrops upon a bamboo shoot. When night fell, the girl with golden eyes and the boy stopped to spend the night. She told him ancient legends that no one had ever heard. In the distant past, before Liyue was founded and the Geo Archon was born, three moons shone in the sky, three sisters. The moons were daughters of prose and song, sovereign over the night sky. They navigated the heavens above in their silver carriage, alternating with one another thrice a month. The three sisters shared one love, the stars of daybreak. Only at the fleeting moments when day and night converged could one of the three sisters pass the fading stars and gaze upon the chambers of the morning stars. The three sisters loved their chosen one with equal sincerity, and they loved each other just as sincerely. And so they lived until the day of the catastrophe that turned the world upside down. The sovereign chariots overturned, and the moon palaces crumbled. The three sisters of the night turned against one another, leading to their eternal parting by death. Only one of their pale corpses now remains, ever shedding its cold light. From then on, the wolf packs, children of the moons, lamented the fate of their mother with each new moon. And so those who live among the wolves call upon the morning stars, the surviving love of the moon, the grievous stars. When the boy awoke to the sunlight, the bamboo forest was bathed in sunlight and shrouded in wisps of morning mist, like a fluttering horsetail. The woman held his hand, and together they walked toward the place where the sun pierced through the woods. Along undergrowth teeming with insects, clambering over slippery moss-covered stones, scaling down a gorge hidden by the shadows of the bamboo trees. As they parted, the boy asked the name of the woman in white, but she only laughed and said nothing. The boy set off for the thriving Liyue Harbor, and the woman stood silently at the boundaries of the bamboo forest, her bewitching golden eyes seeming to have long foreseen the boy's fate. In the dawn's glow, the boy heard a whinnying cry that then grew distant. When he turned around, there was no one behind him, only a single strand of hair that had come to rest on his shoulder. Many years later, the boy, who was a boy no longer, would remember that moment, and he would understand: the gap between them was like a yawning chasm. His fate was to leave his home and go to Liyue Harbor, to seek the riches the Geo Archon had bestowed upon him. Hers, then, was to hide herself away, away from the majestic, kindly gaze of that great Lord of Geo, and protect those ancient tales that even she was beginning to forget.

The second legend tells of a young man who journeyed to the valley of hidden jade to cultivate his arts, only to unexpectedly encounter an Adeptus one night as she, too, passed through those same woods. She wore a long white cotton robe, a pearly raincoat and hat, and her eyes were dazzling and gentle, yet indifferent. Her voice was elegant and tranquil, like jade that falls into a clear spring. She told him stories of distant times, and they enchanted him so much that he forgot the moon's rise and fall, the cycle and orbit of the stars, the first croaks of frogs and cries of the cicadas at dawn. The woman in white robes took him on a tour of secluded abodes where Adepti dwelled, and there had him watch an unfinished game of chess; to the bottom of a clear river, exploring the courts of deceased deities; and up steep cliffs that overlooked the desolate cities left behind by the mountain tribes. They explored the dreams of the fish that played beneath the springs, and they danced together like the ancestral mages who revered the serpent, accompanying the demons and gods of the mountain in falling into deep slumber only when the cicadas had fallen silent. Yet despite this, the young man grew sad. Mortals were transient guests between the heavens and earth, and thus they were inclined to momentary feelings. But the young man wondered what an Adeptus would think of such a lovely night. The woman gave him a smile, and her eyes squinted to slits, but she decided to satisfy his curiosity. The Adepti experienced time differently than mortals. In her eyes, time was a barren wasteland with neither beginning nor end, blanketed in spider-silk threads that stretched to unknowable distances. Everything walks or runs — even mountains, motionless to mortal sight, may dissipate like rolling clouds in hers. Even mercury, which mortals hold to be enduring, through her amber-gold eyes can be seen to wear, tear, and collapse, not to mention fleeting troubles or love. But she sprinted forever alongside all movements, shattered every wave, and dispersed all sediment, caring only to run from this moment into the future. The mountain people once viewed her as time's daughter, like a white horse leaping from a pure spring, one whom no shackles could bind. Just as it was with her proud mother, so it was with her — no wall or eggshell could bar her path. The shepherds of the plains once pursued her steps, freeing themselves from the fetters of the wilderness, embarking on a migratory search for the waterweeds, and thus did the golden-white foal blaze the trail for all herds in the land. The kingdom of the ocean depths once saw her as an emissary, and based on their imagination, they granted her scales and tail plumage, falling down in worship of the light brought by one who was both mother and daughter. In the days when mortals received the blessings of the heavens, great heroes and wandering champions would visit the clear springs for her blessing, fighting over the tenderness she left in her hurried wake. But when the moon palace collapsed, the chariot fell, and the three moon sisters were slain, these legends were lost alongside disaster's descent and the downfall of bygone peoples. The heavens rained down cruel order, and from that day, the stars stilled their orbits, and the earth ceased to turn. Trapped within the shell of the starry sky, she was forced to tarry within this stagnant, foreign land, awaiting her mother's thousand threads, awaiting the erosion of hardy stone, awaiting the next encounter from beyond. When the golden-eyed woman finished her story, the young man asked her name, but she only laughed. Many years later, the young man, now old and grey, recalled this moment by chance. By then, he had honed his swordplay to flow like water, founded his own sect, and became a teacher — and still, he never could comprehend the final story she told him. And as for her, she sprints still along the threads of fate, concealing her trail beneath the forests and springs, far from the gaze of the gods, guarding the ancient stories that slip away from even her.

According to another legend, the White Horse Adeptus encountered a girl in the forest who was gathering herbs to sell for her ailing mother when she slipped on a cliff and fell. Zijiao threw the herbs to the fish and offered to tell the girl a story in exchange, which she could sell at a bookstore. The Adeptus told her how, long ago, when three moons still shone in the sky, the kingdom of Lang-Gan flourished under their light. This kingdom was the home of a divine
who blessed these lands with gentle winds and generous rains. In gratitude, the people revered her as a Goddess of Soil and Grain. But when the moons crumbled, and the kingdom lay in ruins, the divine emissary could not accept this fate and granted the people protection. She led the surviving people to the east, where they found a new home. However, for disobeying the will of heaven, the divine messenger was imprisoned in the skies, never to see the human world again. After finishing her story, the White Horse Adeptus said she had made it up and that it was time for the girl to go home. Suddenly, a wind blew through the forest, and the Adeptus disappeared. The girl took off running, and when she left the forest, her ruined home appeared before her, as if hundreds of years had passed. Afterward, the girl woke up where she had fallen, with her basket filled with the herbs she had gathered. Just when she thought the incident had been a dream, a white horse suddenly galloped over the cliff. The girl grew up and told her story to the descendants of the Lu family, who later opened the Baiju Guesthouse in honor of the White Horse Adeptus.

In ancient times, people believed that lunar eclipses were manifestations of the Zhanzhu — toad-like creatures dwelling in the heavens. Each one was plump and bloated, like a warty, overfed toad, and they possessed a strange magic that allowed them to steal people's wishes and even the essence of the moon itself. It was believed that on Lantern Rite, when the lanterns first glow and the full moon shines its brightest, the world is awash in silver light. But to the eyes of those Zhanzhu, the full moon is nothing but a giant, round pancake, waiting to be gnawed and misused for their mischief. One day, Zhanzhu the Moon Devourer opened his blood-red maw and let out a long howl, then swallowed the full moon in one gulp, like a rice ball, and it vanished into his stomach. At that moment, the world was plunged into darkness, and the little Zhanzhu moved at their master's command, rushing forth to wreak havoc. Suddenly, the White Horse Adeptus appeared, who, according to ancient legends, lived on the moon and was older than the Geo Archon himself. Deprived of moonlight, she found herself surrounded by countless demons. When defeat seemed inevitable, the villagers of Chenyu Vale released the festival's Xiao Lanterns into the sky, lighting up the heavens to aid the Adeptus in battle.

There is also a legend about the Second Deadly Self, Zizhi. Thousands of years ago, when The Chasm, where the kingdom of Lang-Gan once stood, was attacked by the dragon Azhdaha, the daughter of the sheer cliffs and crystal sands, set out in search of the Adeptus who forged swords from flowing light and once vanished into the watery moon beneath the depths. Seeking the sword that would save them from calamity, the girl, following ancient songs, reached a kingdom hidden in a cavern. There, she encountered a silver shadow. Hearing the girl's purpose, the shadow seemed to laugh, rippling along with the spring under the moon. The shadowed figure pulled a wild bamboo stalk from the slanted cliff. The tip broke and fell, but the girl caught it before it touched the ground. <color=#ffffffd9>"As the waxing moon bears its light, one might chase forms and shadows. Now, now... You've understood the true essence of the sword. Why seek its physical form, then?"</color> Upon her return, the girl trained a hundred elite warriors in the art of sword and spear, and together with the Lord of Geo, they tamed the dragon and established peace in all four directions. Her tribe, casting aside their warlike roots, followed Rex Lapis to the east, becoming the Shenglu Hall.
